definition: A generative probabilistic model used for topic modeling, where each document is modeled as a mixture of latent topics and each topic as a distribution over words.
details: LDA was one of the most influential topic modeling techniques in the pre-deep-learning era of NLP, and remains a useful baseline for unsupervised text analysis.

explainer.lead: Latent Dirichlet Allocation is a generative probabilistic topic model in which each document is a mixture of latent topics and each topic a distribution over words. It was one of the most influential topic-modeling techniques of the pre-deep-learning NLP era.

tiers.eli5: Imagine every article is a blend of a few themes, and every theme is a blend of favourite words. The model works out both blends just from the words in the articles.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for unsupervised text analysis and as a baseline for topic modeling. Treat it as a baseline rather than a state-of-the-art method; it belongs to the pre-deep-learning era.
tiers.paperLevel: A generative probabilistic model for topic modeling: each document is modeled as a mixture of latent topics, and each topic as a distribution over words. Its influence dates to the pre-deep-learning era of NLP, where it remains a useful baseline for unsupervised text analysis.

explainer.example: Given a corpus of news articles, the model assigns each article a mix of topics and each topic a ranked distribution over words.
